summary: An ancilla-assisted gate-based protocol enhances sensitivity to hidden photon kinetic mixing using a single two-qubit entangling gate on NISQ devices, achieving up to 10-fold reduction in integration time compared to Rabi-sampling experiments. Under realistic noise with three years of data taking, the projected exclusion limit on the mixing parameter reaches $\varepsilon \approx 1 \times 10^{-14}$ across $2.5$–$6.0$ GHz ($10$–$25$ µeV).
motivation: Direct dark matter detection via transmon qubits requires either maintaining long-lived multi-qubit entangled states or accepting reduced sensitivity; this work exploits the fact that weak Rabi oscillations from hidden photons on the qubit can be enhanced with modest gate fidelity ($>99\%$) without such constraints.
method: After a sensing qubit interacts with dark matter for time $\tau \sim 100$ µs, a CNOT, X-gate, and controlled-$R_Y(\beta)$ gate transform the state; post-selection on ancilla collapse to $|1_A\rangle$ creates signal amplification via $P_\sim \propto \sin^{-2}(\beta/2) \, P_e$ for small excitation probability $P_e$, with noise model including $T_1$, $T_\phi$, thermal occupation, and readout/preparation errors.
result: Speedup factor $\mathcal{G} = 4$–$6$ achieved when readout error $r \gtrsim 2\%$ and preparation error $p \lesssim 0.3\%$; scaling to $n$ sensing qubits coupled sequentially to one ancilla gives $\mathcal{G} \to 2\mathcal{G}$ asymptotically, reaching $\sim 10$-fold enhancement with 120 physical qubits in realistic hardware regimes.
